examples.text: Mit Beginn der nächsten Woche brach man denn auch wirklich auf, und am selben Abend noch war man in Saßnitz.
examples.ref: 1896, Theodor Fontane, chapter 24, in Effi Briest, Berlin: F. Fontane & Co.:
examples.english: At the beginning of the next week they finally departed, and on the same evening they arrived in Saßnitz.
examples.translation: At the beginning of the next week they finally departed, and on the same evening they arrived in Saßnitz.

examples.text: Es ist Abend, und vor den Fenstern ihres Wohnzimmers liegt der Central Park in tiefes Dunkel gehüllt.
examples.ref: 1996 April 30, Patrick Conley, “Die vergessene Tradition”, in SFB3, archived from the original on 26 Mar 2014:
examples.english: It is evening, and past the windows of her living room, Central Park is wrapped in deep darkness.
examples.translation: It is evening, and past the windows of her living room, Central Park is wrapped in deep darkness.

raw.etymology_text:
From Middle High German ābent, from Old High German āband, from Proto-West Germanic *ābanþ, from Proto-Germanic *ēbanþs.
Compare Low German Avend, Dutch avond, English eve, even (evening), Old Norse aptann, Swedish afton, Norwegian and Danish aften.
